steps.description: Given a fake clock and a service with updates built in, when it runs, then it checks a minute after it starts, every 4 hours and after a resume past 4 hours; it asks the beta address only under the beta policy; it never checks with Updates = 0 or in a build without a key; and on a metered network it downloads only an urgent version.
Given a check, when the request the service sends is read, then it is one HTTPS GET of the channel's fixed address, with no query, no cookie, no identifier and the User-Agent `thermi`.

Given an update folder and a version that passes every check, when anything fails one check instead (the manifest, the zip, what the zip holds, a release build's catalog, or the folder's access), then nothing under the folder changes, no version runs and the event log has a warning or an error; and the version that passes every check is taken.

Given an installed version and a manifest, when the service plans, then it takes only a higher version that has not failed here, is not withdrawn and whose rollout reaches the PC's number; raising the rollout adds PCs and drops none; and when the installed version is withdrawn, the PC goes back to the kept previous version if that one is older, not withdrawn and has not failed, and otherwise stays.

Given a version ready, when a session has its window open, a drag under way or input within three minutes, then it is not quiet; when it has none of them and is idle for three minutes, locked or has every overlay hidden, then it is quiet; and an urgent version waits only for the window and the drag.

Given an install folder with a process running from its launcher and a switch written down, when the switch is cut at any of its steps and the service starts again, then the launchers and the service's image path name either the old version or the new one whole, the running process goes on, the next start runs the version the switch left, and only folders of versions neither kept nor running are deleted.

Given a switch in probation, when the new service serves no snapshot in 120 polls, or a second run of it ends without stopping within 10 minutes, then the PC goes back to the previous version and never takes the failed one again; a sleep of any length in between fails nothing; and an overlay that cannot switch gives up after 60 of its ticks.
Given settings a newer version wrote, with the earlier format's copy kept beside them, when the earlier version reads them, then it reads its copy and keeps the newer file beside it.
Given settings of this version holding a member it does not know in each of their objects, when an edit is made and undone, then each written file still holds every one of them.
Given a recording, when the service writes its pipe's lines for it, then they are the golden file's, byte for byte.

Given channels with history, when the owner publishes, promotes, rolls back, turns a channel off and signs it again, then each makes the next signed manifest, expiring 45 days later; a version below the channel's is refused; stable passing beta lifts beta; and a rollback withdraws the version and offers the one before it.

Given each state of the updates, when About shows it, then its line says up to date and when, a version ready, turned off by policy, the beta channel, no check for 14 days, or a build that does not update itself.
Given a check that finds a version, a download, a switch, a rollback and a refusal, when each happens, then the event log has one entry for it under thermi-sensors.

Given About asked for a check, when it reads the state, then it says it checks until the service has checked since a minute before the ask, for half a minute at most, and then says up to date, checked just now, or names the version ready, offering a restart only when its switch is not held.

Given About's last ask, never made, made less or more than a minute ago, or made ahead of a clock set back, when the service hears a new ask, then it checks at once, except within a minute of the last ask; a clock set back behind the last ask holds nothing off.
Given a version ready right after a quiet session's code, when About's restart asks for it while a check runs, then the switch begins once the check ends.

Given the service installed or not, and a user's pipe whose owner, server process or label passes or fails one of the overlay's checks, when the overlay picks a pipe, then it reads the service's whenever the service is installed, and the user's only when every check passes.

Given the user's host started as the user, when an overlay connects and later leaves, then the host serves the same lines on the pipe named for the user's SID, owned by that SID and closed to other users and remote clients, stays 10 s after its last client left and then ends with the Stopped mark; and a host no client came to ends after 30 s.

Given a per-user install's host and a channel offering a machine MSI, when it is asked to install for everyone, then msiexec starts only for the file the manifest names, with its bytes and, in a release build, thermi's signature, held open while it runs and under the updater's lock; a refused prompt is written as refused and runs nothing that follows a good install; a manifest that cannot be read, other bytes or an unsigned MSI change nothing and fail; the policy Updates = 0 opens the download page; and each outcome is written for the window, but not over a switch under way.

Given a per-user install and a channel offering a newer version, when the user's host checks, then it takes the version by the service's rules, only into a folder that no one but the user, SYSTEM and administrators may write, and switches through its own watchdog, run as the user.

Given the user's host serving a client, or waiting while another program holds its pipe's name, when the watchdog sets its stop event, then it ends; and given an event of its name that someone else made first, then the host does not run, so no other process steers it.
Given a version published with its MSIs, when the manifest is read, then each processor's machine MSI has its URL, size and SHA-256, and a manifest without them still reads.
Given the machine MSI's source, when its driver action is read, then ADDDRIVER is a secure property and the action runs only under NOT Installed AND ADDDRIVER = 1, so no repair adds the driver.

Given hosts that ended long after their start or soon after it, and a switch's lock held, when the overlay finds no host, then it waits 2 s, doubling up to a minute after hosts that ended within 10 s of their start, and starts none while the lock is held.

Given a manifest that offers the running version, a later one, an earlier one or none, or a channel turned off or withdrawing the running version, when the fix picks the machine MSI, then it takes only the MSI of the version offered, when that is the running one or later, for this processor, and otherwise none, which opens the download page.

Given a real pipe with no label and one labelled low, as a sandboxed process makes it, when the overlay reads its server, then it reads the server's image and integrity as Windows has them, and the pipe's label as medium and as low.
Given the pinned driver or a later one already installed, when the elevated service's install-driver runs, then it downloads and runs nothing and only starts the sensors again.

Given the state's last sequence, when the service plans with a manifest of another channel, of an older sequence, expired, or expiring more than 45 days and a day ahead, then it refuses it; and it takes one of the same sequence, one expiring now and one expiring 46 days ahead.
Given a downloaded file, when the service checks it against the package, then only a file of the package's size and SHA-256 is the package, and a refusal names the size or the hash that differs.
Given a zip's entries, when the service unpacks it, then only entries that land inside the version's folder pass, and rooted entries, drives, streams, climbs out and links are refused.

Given the user's host asked to install for everyone, when the policy turns updates off, the manifest cannot be read, or the channel offers no MSI for the running version or later, then the policy and the missing MSI open the download page and the unreadable manifest fails; and only an MSI the channel offers runs.

Given an envelope the service opens, when it is too large, not an envelope, signed by no key built into thermi, or signed by the release key after the backup key revoked it, then it is refused; and only the backup key revokes the release key, naming it, and sets the sequence back, once.

Given msiexec's exit code after the UAC prompt, when the user's host reads it, then success and success needing a restart are installed, a refused prompt and a cancel are refused, and any other code is a failure.

Given both MSIs' source, when their custom actions are read, then each runs its program through the util extension's DLL native to the package's processor, with its command line in a property of its own set before it, as WixQuietExec or, for the overlay, WixUnelevatedShellExec run immediate and impersonated, and none as a plain executable action.

Given a signed program and an unsigned catalog, when thermi checks who signed them, then it trusts the program by its signer's thumbprint, never by a name another certificate could carry, and refuses the unsigned catalog.
Given the per-user MSI's source, when the machine's overlay looks for the per-user product to remove, then the UpgradeCode it looks for is the one the per-user MSI is built with.
